geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the single cantilevered block with a split-wing macro so the mass can open a legible public seam toward the access edge and better satisfy neighborhood-living public threshold logic.
Split along the plan axis to create an actual courtyard/entry gap rather than a topological fracture.
Make the void proportion large enough to read as public ground but small enough to preserve one dominant architectural body.
Maintain continuity across the split so the composition remains a unified building rather than two detached fragments.
Ensure the base retains an active ground element suitable for a neighborhood mixed-use threshold.
Keep the ground spine low enough to feel public and porous.
Preserve a clear occupied edge without closing off the access side.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant gesture away from a sealed cantilevered block toward a split-wing mass that can host a real public threshold on the access edge while preserving the main body in ancestry.
Align the split to the horizontal plan logic so the new void can register as a street-facing gap rather than a purely vertical sculptural cut.
Create a readable public seam/entry slot without over-fragmenting the mass.
Keep the two wings related so the composition remains one dominant gesture rather than separate fragments.
Preserve an occupiable ground condition at the base to support the active frontage requirement.
Strengthen the street-edge datum while leaving enough void for entry/public use.

rationale: The candidate reads as one primary mass, but it is not yet convincing as neighborhood living. Across views the object is coherent enough, but the dominant form feels like an inwardly compressed wedge/cap rather than a mixed-use street building with an active ground threshold. The most visible problem is the lack of a legible public void on the access edge: the blue frontage is met by a mostly sealed side, with no clear entry seam, court, or undercut. The silhouette is moderately resolved, but the section logic is arbitrary and slightly stair-like without a strong inhabitable terrace or daylight/spatial consequence. Because the program context asks for compact capacity with active ground edge and one clear public void or terrace, the current mass falls short of program fit even though it has some formal continuity and a bounded parcel response.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing with a carved entry/void and layered ground-public relation.
Courtyard-forward neighborhood building: the void is the organizing public figure, not a leftover.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but the access-edge response is weak.
Solids do not visibly collide across views, but the current form reads as over-compressed and not meaningfully public at grade.
The mass is coherent in more than one view, so this is not a total structural failure; it is a program/section failure.
Site access is on the west in the program frame; the candidate does not clearly open the matching edge.
